[IALC.7.1] An override (a `DS_ALLOC_WEAK` strong definition or
`DS_ALLOC_MACRO` `DS_ALLOC_HEADER` macros) must match libc semantics,
because libds relies on them:

- `ds_free(NULL)` / `DS_FREE(NULL)` is a no-op.
- `ds_realloc(NULL, n)` equals `malloc(n)`; `ds_realloc(p, 0)` follows
  libc.
- `ds_calloc(n, s)` zero-initialises and checks `n*s` for overflow.
- `ds_malloc(0)` returns `NULL` or a freeable pointer; libds handles
  either.
- `ds_strdup`/`ds_strndup` return layer-owned memory freeable by
  `ds_free`. libds never calls `DS_STRDUP(NULL)`.
- Returned memory must be aligned to `max_align_t`.
